item.title: HugeGraph Server Quick Start
item.description:
1 HugeGraph Server Overview

apache/hugegraph is the main repository for the HugeGraph graph database. Its top-level modules include hugegraph-server, hugegraph-pd, and hugegraph-store. This page describes the hugegraph-server module and the service it runs.

The hugegraph-server module contains hugegraph-core, hugegraph-api, hugegraph-dist, and storage adapters. Core implements the property graph model, transactions, and TinkerPop interfaces. API provides the HTTP service and delegates client requests to Core. Graph data is stored in RocksDB (the default standalone backend), HStore (distributed), or HBase.

item.title: HugeGraph-PD Quick Start
item.description:
1 HugeGraph-PD Overview

HugeGraph-PD (Placement Driver) is the metadata management component of HugeGraph’s distributed version, responsible for managing the distribution of graph data and coordinating storage nodes. It plays a central role in distributed HugeGraph, maintaining cluster status and coordinating HugeGraph-Store storage nodes.

PD keeps cluster metadata in an embedded RocksDB store under pd.data-path and replicates it across PD nodes with Raft, so a 3-node or 5-node PD cluster keeps serving while a minority of nodes is down. On top of that it registers and activates Store nodes, allocates and rebalances partitions, tracks Store heartbeats, and answers service discovery queries from Store and Server.

item.title: HugeGraph-Store Quick Start
item.description:
1 HugeGraph-Store Overview

HugeGraph-Store is the storage node component of HugeGraph’s distributed version, responsible for actually storing and managing graph data. It works in conjunction with HugeGraph-PD to form HugeGraph’s distributed storage engine, providing high availability and horizontal scalability.

Each Store node keeps graph data in RocksDB and replicates it with Raft (JRaft): every partition is a separate Raft group, so a partition survives the loss of a minority of its replicas. Store nodes do not know about each other directly. They register with PD, receive their partition assignment from PD, and report state back over a heartbeat. HugeGraph-Server reaches Store over gRPC after looking up partition locations in PD.

item.title: Deploy HugeGraph with Helm
item.description:
This guide follows the chart in the HugeGraph development branch. Image tags remain latest until release images are published; pin images for your installation. The chart requires Helm 3 and Kubernetes 1.23 or later. Start with the chart README for common commands and settings. Advanced lifecycle procedures are in the operations reference.

1 Install

Note

Default Topology & Storage Prerequisites

  • Components: Deploys 3 PD + 3 Store + 3 Server and Hubble by default, with authentication and persistent storage enabled.
  • Volume Requirements: Requires a default dynamic StorageClass or matching pre-created static PVs, totaling 7 persistent volumes (3 × 10 GiB PD volumes, 3 × 50 GiB Store volumes, and 1 × 1 GiB Hubble volume).
  • Memory Sizing: Retains container JVM memory auto-calculation; configure resource requests/limits to allocate sufficient physical memory for the 9 JVMs and Hubble.
 1git clone https://github.com/apache/hugegraph.git
 2cd hugegraph
 3kubectl config current-context
 4kubectl get nodes
 5kubectl get storageclass
 6# Standard cluster deployment (3 PD + 3 Store + 3 Server + 1 Hubble; requires 7 PVs):
 7helm install hugegraph ./helm/hugegraph -n hugegraph \
 8 --create-namespace --wait --timeout 15m
 9
10# Local testing or single-node environments (Minikube, Kind; 1 replica and no anti-affinity):
11# helm install hugegraph ./helm/hugegraph -n hugegraph \
12# -f ./helm/hugegraph/values-single.yaml \
13# --create-namespace --wait --timeout 10m

2 Modes and entry points 

helm/hugegraph/
 Chart.yaml # Chart metadata and version definitions
 values.yaml # Default values (easy mode: 3 PD + 3 Store + 3 Server + 1 Hubble, NodePort)
 values-single.yaml # Single-node preset (local Minikube/Kind testing with 1 replica and no anti-affinity)
 values-cluster.yaml # Multi-node cluster preset (required anti-affinity, Store OnDelete rollout)
 values-strict.yaml # Hardened security preset (strict mode: ClusterIP only, strict NetworkPolicies)
 values.schema.json # Schema validation for values configuration
 templates/ # Kubernetes workload templates
 pd-statefulset.yaml # PD StatefulSet (metadata and scheduling)
 store-statefulset.yaml # Store StatefulSet (storage engine)
 server-deployment.yaml # Server Deployment (injects serviceId and graphSpace)
 hubble-deployment.yaml # Hubble UI Deployment
 tests/ # Smoke validation hook (helm test, supports custom testGraphAlias)
 examples/ # Seven complete production scenario examples (local PVs, GitOps secrets, Ingress)
 docs/operations.md # Lifecycle operations and recovery guide

mode: easy is the default. Server and Hubble use automatic NodePorts; PD stays ClusterIP. HTTP works without a domain, certificate or acknowledgement. mode: strict defaults Server/Hubble to ClusterIP and enables NetworkPolicy. Both modes keep authentication and persistence. Explicit component parameters take priority over global parameters, which take priority over mode defaults; explicit false remains an override. The global parameters are persistence.enabled and global.imageRegistry. Strict mode is also available through values-strict.yaml.

item.title: Operate HugeGraph on Kubernetes
item.description:
This guide accompanies Helm deployment. Detailed lifecycle checks and recovery notes are maintained in the operations reference; all parameters are commented in values.yaml. Commands assume release/namespace hugegraph; substitute the actual workload names if overridden.

1 Storage and private images

The default installation needs seven persistent volumes. Dynamic storage requires a working provisioner; static local storage requires prepared directories and matching PVs on the named nodes. Use the complete examples for all seven local PVs, WaitForFirstConsumer, registry mirrors and GitOps Secrets. An initially Pending PVC with WaitForFirstConsumer can be normal; persistent Pending needs PVC/Pod events and PV matching checks. A bound claim with a missing directory or permission mismatch can fail mounting. Do not replace failed PVCs with temporary data directories.
